title: A Bakery for the Postcard
premise: Ulyana Montrose inherited her family's failing vineyard along with its crushing debts, and the only thing she loves more cautiously than the land is Theo Marchand, the baker whose seaside shop once appeared on a postcard she's kept for ten years. When her estranged family summons her to a reunion where her inheritance—and her single status—will be scrutinized, she asks Theo to pose as her boyfriend, an arrangement that stops being pretend somewhere between the toasts and the dessert course. But their fake romance collides with an old injustice: the forged signature that stripped Theo's family of the very vineyard Ulyana now owns, a truth her relatives buried a decade ago. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Ulyana must choose between the loyalty that kept her silent and the truth that could save them both, finally saying the sentence she has rehearsed since the night the postcard arrived.
about_author: Marguerite Amberdale is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded early-morning ovens for late-night manuscripts, writing love stories set in coastal towns where everyone knows your order. She lives above a bookshop with a sourdough starter older than most of her relationships.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Soil
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She walks her debt-laden vineyard at dawn, cataloguing what the bank could seize, and finds the ten-year-old postcard of Theo's bakery hidden in her desk—the one memento she never explains. Emotional beat: weary tenderness, the ache of loving something you can't afford to keep.

chapters.title: Flour and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He closes his bakery after a slow morning, pretending not to notice Ulyana's truck parked outside his shop every Tuesday for years. Their careful, wordless ritual of bread-for-grapes is interrupted by the reunion invitation she's been avoiding. Emotional beat: longing disguised as routine.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Ivory
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Montrose reunion summons arrives with a lawyer's letterhead—her aunt wants the vineyard's future settled, and unattached heirs get sidelined. Panicked, Ulyana drives to the bakery and, before she can stop herself, asks Theo to be her fake boyfriend. Emotional beat: reckless hope tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions of the Heart
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He agrees, but negotiates one condition she can't yet understand: that she owes him one honest answer before the season's last ferry. They practice being a couple over closing-time wine, and the pretending is alarmingly easy. Emotional beat: playful tension shadowed by an unspoken debt.

chapters.title: Arrivals at Montrose House
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The reunion begins; her aunt Vivienne greets Theo with a smile that falters a half-second too long, and a cousin's drunk joke about 'the Marchand name' lands strangely. Ulyana realizes her family remembers more about the bakery than she does. Emotional beat: unease beneath performance.

chapters.title: The Toast That Went Wrong
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At dinner, Vivienne toasts the vineyard's 'clean history,' and Theo's glass trembles—he recognizes the phrasing from a court document his father never stopped quoting. He plays the charming boyfriend flawlessly while quietly confirming his suspicions. Emotional beat: charm as armor over old grief.

chapters.title: Dessert and the First Slip
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Over dessert, Theo takes her hand and the fake date stops feeling fake; she almost says something true and swallows it. Later, she catches Vivienne and the family lawyer whispering over a box of old files. Emotional beat: the moment pretending becomes dangerous.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Exploring the cellar, Theo finds crates of records and a deed bearing his grandfather's signature—dated three days after the old man's death. He photographs it and says nothing, testing whether Ulyana's family loyalty runs deeper than her feelings for him. Emotional beat: cold clarity, love under interrogation.

chapters.title: A Walk on the Bluff
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Theo asks her, casually, what she knows about how the Montroses acquired the north parcel. She defends her family too quickly and too loudly, and they part on the bluff with the fake relationship cracking under real weight. Emotional beat: the first real fight.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo checks the season's last ferry—nine days out—and sets it as his private deadline: tell Ulyana everything, or leave with his family's grievance and his heart intact. Meanwhile Vivienne offers him money to 'keep things simple.' Emotional beat: a clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Grapes, Crushed and Confessed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Harvest work throws them together; exhausted and honest in the dark of the crush pad, Theo tells her the deed is forged and her inheritance was built on his family's ruin. Ulyana's world tilts—the vineyard she loves is stolen goods. Emotional beat: betrayal and vertigo.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ulyana finally shows him the postcard—she's kept it a decade because the day it arrived was the day she decided not to ask questions about her family's money. He realizes she's been paying penance in silence all along. Emotional beat: grief recognized, intimacy deepened.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Version
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana confronts her aunt, who spins a self-pitying tale: the forgery was her late husband's doing, done to save the family from bankruptcy, and exposing it now would bankrupt Ulyana instead. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of staying silent.

chapters.title: The Offer She Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Vivienne privately offers Theo the bakery's mortgage paid off and a quiet settlement if he drops the deed and leaves before the ferry. He refuses, but realizes Ulyana's family will bury the truth with or without her consent. Emotional beat: temptation declined, stakes raised.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Vines
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A storm threatens the harvest; Ulyana and Theo work side by side through the night saving the grapes, their bodies remembering what their words keep denying. At dawn, half-drowned and laughing, they finally kiss for real. Emotional beat: surrender.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The tenderness of the night before curdles when Theo learns Ulyana met with the family lawyer—she's been offered a restructured loan that survives only if the deed stays buried. He accuses her of choosing the vineyard over justice. Emotional beat: love and principle at war.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana torn: exposing the forgery means losing everything her parents left her; hiding it means losing Theo and becoming her aunt. She spends a sleepless night with the postcard, understanding at last that she's been rehearsing a sentence for ten years and never said it. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Reunion's Last Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Final reunion night; Vivienne plans to announce the vineyard's transfer to a cousin. Theo decides he'll speak the truth publicly rather than let the ferry leave with it, even if it costs him Ulyana. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Before Theo can stand, Ulyana rises and says it—the sentence rehearsed for a decade: that her family's fortune was stolen, that she kept the postcard and her silence, and that she's done with both. The room erupts; she takes Theo's hand in front of everyone. Emotional beat: catharsis, the decade-long debt paid.

chapters.title: Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Disowned and disbelieving, Ulyana and Theo race to the dock as the season's final ferry loads. He asks if she understands what she's given up; she answers with the truth instead of reassurance. They board together—not fleeing, but choosing. Emotional beat: leap of faith.

chapters.title: Justice, Slow as Bread
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Winter: the forgery goes before a mediator; the north parcel is returned to the Marchand family, and Ulyana keeps the vineyard by selling the Montrose house to pay the debts honestly. Vivienne leaves in disgrace; Ulyana feels lighter, not poorer. Emotional beat: justice outside the courtroom, grief and relief entwined.

chapters.title: A Bakery for the Postcard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring: Theo and Ulyana merge vineyard and bakery into one small enterprise, and a new postcard is printed—their own storefront, grapes on one side, bread on the other. Ulyana mails it to no one; it's a promise, not a memory. Emotional beat: homecoming, love in the present tense.
